notes: Peaky beachbreak; guides say all tides, behaviour depends on swell size and sandbanks. No source splits by swell size.
Best at mid tide on NW swell, but a wave at any tide; rising tide preferred. Strong currents at spring tides.

avoid: height > 3.2 or (height < 1.5 and swell >= 1.5) or swell > 2.5
notes: Small waves: rising low tide or falling mid tide; no waves at high tide (with big coefficients, none from 2 h before high). Big waves (>1.5 m): rising mid tide, because at low tide the spot saturates and the bar is hard to cross. 2 h after low = fast shortboard waves, 2 h after high = soft longboard waves. Works at all tides overall.

Best with swell >1.5 m, period >10 s, offshore wind. All tides except high with big coefficients and/or small swell. Surf'In Landes says rising low tide is best; World Beach Guide says low to outgoing (conflict on direction). Breaks on very little depth: dangerous. Holds 3 m+.
Only works in strong swell (breaks 100 m+ offshore); at its best in winter. All tides except high with big coefficients; low tide best with small coefficients, low→mid with big coefficients.

Around low tide with small coefficients, low→mid with big coefficients; around high tide no waves or closing shorebreak. Low = shortboard, mid = longboard. Gentler than other Hossegor spots. Same site's spot guide: big swell → rising mid tide.

Low tide with small coefficients, low→mid with big coefficients; past mid tide it turns into hard-to-catch shorebreak. Swell over 1–1.5 m for manoeuvrable waves; sheltered fallback spot, fast short waves. Older sources disagreed (one mentioned high tide).

avoid: height > 4.2 or (height > 3.2 and swell < 1) or swell > 3.5
notes: Small/medium swell: low→mid tide. Waves over 1 m with small coefficients: all tides work, even high. Filters long/big (winter, N, >15 s period) swells and handles small swells well; best sandbanks in Capbreton.

Best around mid tide; low tide good in small swell, high tide good in big swell, but high tide + big coefficient + medium/big swell = violent shorebreak. Catches swell best in Capbreton; for good surfers. Older sources also said rising tide.
